module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 15

References:
- [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.15)
- [BJP14] T. Brown, V. Jungić and A. Poelstra, "On double 3-term arithmetic progressions",
  Integers 14 (2014), Paper No. A43.
- [CCS14] J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, "Avoidance of additive cubes and
  related results", Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace Green15

/--
Does there exist a Lipschitz function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$ whose graph
$\Gamma = \{(n, f(n)) : n \in \mathbb{N}\} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}^2$ is free of 3-term progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 3 := by
  sorry

/--
The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [BJP14].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_15_ap4 :
    ∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ f : ℕ → ℤ, LipschitzWith K f ∧
      IsAPOfLengthFree  {((n, f n) : ℤ × ℤ) | (n : ℕ)} 4 := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add finitary version

end Green15

findings.description: The docstring credits the 4-term result to [BJP14] ("The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [BJP14]."). The cited source credits it to Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer and Shallit, the file's [CCS14]. BJP14 is mentioned there only as a paper that has considered the problem, and BJP14 itself credits CCS for the 4-term fact. [CCS14] is listed in the module docstring but never used in any declaration docstring. The Lean statement is correct and true; only the citation is off.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 open problems, Problem 15 comments (https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf): "It has recently been considered in print by Brown, Jungić and Poelstra [58]. The answer is yes for 4-term progressions. This is established by Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer and Shallit [65], who write in the language of combinatorics on words. They construct an infinite word x1x2x3··· in the alphabet {0,1,3,4} which avoids 'additive cubes' ... One may then define f(n) = x1+···+xn." BJP14 (Integers 14 (2014) A43, p. 3): "The existence of an infinite word on four integers with no additive cubes ... established by Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit [4], translates into the fact that there is an increasing sequence of positive integers with bounded gaps with no double 4-term arithmetic progression."
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to cite [CCS14], e.g. "The answer is YES for 4-term progressions [CCS14]: take $f(n) = x_1 + \dots + x_n$ for an infinite word $x_1 x_2 \cdots$ over $\{0,1,3,4\}$ that avoids additive cubes."

findings.description: The module docstring cites [CCS14] as "Avoidance of additive cubes and related results", Adv. in Appl. Math. 56 (2014), 25–66. I could not find any such paper. Crossref has no work with that title. Adv. Appl. Math. vol. 56 (2014) has other articles on pp. 1–19, 20–34, 35–55 and 56–77. The paper Green actually cites for this result, with the same four authors, is "Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum", J. ACM 61 (2014).
findings.source_evidence: Green's bibliography entry [65]: "J. Cassaigne, J. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum. J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Art. 10, 17 pp." Crossref: DOI 10.1145/2590775 (J. ACM 61, pp. 1–17). Crossref listing of Adv. Appl. Math. vol. 56 (ISSN 0196-8858) has no paper by these authors. arXiv:1106.5204 has the same title as the J. ACM paper.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the reference with: [CCS14] J. Cassaigne, J. D. Currie, L. Schaeffer and J. Shallit, "Avoiding three consecutive blocks of the same size and same sum", J. ACM 61 (2014), no. 2, Art. 10, 17 pp. (arXiv:1106.5204).

reformulations.difference: Green writes f : ℕ → ℤ but defines the graph as Γ = {(n, f(n)) : n ∈ ℤ}, which is a typo. The Lean takes the graph over n ∈ ℕ (including 0), cast into ℤ × ℤ. It renders "Lipschitz" as ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzWith K f, using Mathlib's metrics on ℕ and ℤ. It renders "free of 3-term progressions" as Set.IsAPOfLengthFree Γ 3, where Set.IsAPOfLength is defined through ENat.card.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (i) Lipschitz: I proved in Lean that LipschitzWith K f ↔ ∀ m n, |f m − f n| ≤ K·|m − n|. By telescoping, this is equivalent to bounded consecutive differences, which is Green's "Lipschitz constant max_n |f(n+1) − f(n)|". (ii) AP-freeness: I proved in Lean, without sorry, that (Γ f).IsAPOfLengthFree 3 ↔ ∀ a d : ℕ, 0 < d → f a + f (a+2d) ≠ 2 f (a+d). The ENat.card = 3 condition forces a nonzero common difference, and a graph cannot contain two points with the same first coordinate. So this is exactly "Γ has no non-trivial 3-term progression". (iii) Domain: ℕ with 0 versus positive integers is handled by the shift n ↦ n+1, which translates the graph and so preserves APs and the Lipschitz constant. For ℕ versus Green's literal ℤ: restricting a function on ℤ gives one on ℕ. Conversely, if f on ℕ is C-Lipschitz with a 3-AP-free graph, the translates g_m(n) = f(n+m) − f(m), for n ≥ −m, take at most 2C|n|+1 values at each n. A diagonal subsequence converges pointwise to a C-Lipschitz g : ℤ → ℤ. Any 3-AP in the graph of g would show up in some g_m, hence in a translate of part of f's graph, which is impossible. So both readings pose the same existence question. The same argument covers green_15_ap4.

review.notes:
Both statements are faithful to the source. The only defects are two citation slips, reported as minor.

Lean checks (scratch files /workspace/review/equiv2.lean and scratch.lean):
- `#print` shows the graph elaborates to `{x | ∃ n : ℕ, ((n : ℤ), f n) = x}`.
- `free_iff` characterizes `(Γ f).IsAPOfLengthFree 3` as above. `#print axioms` shows only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
- `LipschitzWith` on ℕ → ℤ uses the usual metrics |m − n|; the `Nat.dist_eq` / `Int.dist_eq` rewrite went through.
- A constant function's graph is not 3-AP-free, and the graph of the (non-Lipschitz) n ↦ n² is 3-AP-free, so the notion is neither vacuous nor unsatisfiable.

Why the variant is true: the partial sums of the CCS word over {0,1,3,4} are 4-Lipschitz. A 4-term AP in their graph over ℕ is exactly an additive cube in the word, and the word has none. So `green_15_ap4` is true, and its `research solved` tag is right.

The answer slot of `green_15` has the source's polarity: \"Does there exist ...?\" matches `∃ ...`, so it is not a negated conjecture. BJP14 poses the same problem in negated form: does every increasing bounded-gap sequence contain a double 3-AP?

Status: the current Green PDF (with 2025 updates) records no resolution of Problem 15, and CCS14 says additive squares over finite subsets of ℤ remain open. Vukusic (arXiv 2506.21200, June 2025) still calls the additive square problem open, and arXiv searches up to September 2026 found no resolution. So `research open` is consistent with the source.

The finitary version is not formalized (there is a TODO in the file). Omitting it is not a defect.
